statement: Mean sentence length is between 3 and 10 words in 38 of 39 analysed books with text (A Day Out, a 3-4 book of one-line cries, averages 2.4); the longest sentence stays at or under 14 words in 23 of 39 (the others reach 15-27, and 38 in the level-3 Kottavi Raja).

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends: mean 6.9, longest 13. The wordless book is not counted.
2026-10-15: Added 8 books with text (Zuko is wordless, not counted). Book Dash: Bathtub Safari 4.2/10, Khumo 3.2/12, Come Back Cat 3.2/4, Feathered Friends 4.6/8 support; Ga Mohana 6.6/18 contradicts. African Storybook: Chicken and Millipede 6.8/14 supports, Bohlale 8.6/18 contradicts (7-8 band). StoryWeaver: Good Night, Monu 9.9/18 contradicts (rhymed read-aloud couplets).
2026-10-28: +6 support, +2 counter. StoryWeaver: The Lost Ball 5.2/9 supports; Get Down, Rocky! 6.3/17 contradicts. Book Dash: Who Ate My Hat 4.3/6, Let's Go Looking 3.4/6, Clever Pig 3.2/6, A House for Mouse 6.5/9, A Day Out 2.4/5 support the longest-sentence half; Dudu's Hat 8.1/24 contradicts. A Day Out breaks the 'mean at least 3' half, so the statement no longer says 'all'. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-10-28 older-book observation, NOT counted (SOURCES.md keeps populations apart): Millions of Cats (Internet Archive, 1928, Gág, study_only) contradicts (several 25-40-word sentences read from the scans; CLI metrics are inflated by OCR noise).
2026-11-13: +5 support (A Trip to the Tap 7.8/14, Mmawe 4.2/12, Rainbow 4.2/12, Play with Me 6.3/10, Sweet Dreams 6.0/14), +5 counter (Going Places 8.7/18, I Can Do It! 10.0/27, Banzi 5.9/21, Khuzwayo 6.9/18, Alex 5.4/15). All 10 means fall in 3-10; the longest-sentence half now holds in fewer than 60%: the 14-word cap is tighter than many recent Book Dash books, but four of the five over-cap books are 5-6 and the cap applies to 5-6 too, so no change is suggested from this alone. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).
